reasoning: The market prices a near-certainty (99.3%) that Google will publicly release Gemini 3.2 by May 31, 2026. While Google's release cadence is fast (Gemini 2.5 Pro in March 2025, likely 3.0 in late 2025), a 3.2 release by May 2026 requires an unbroken series of two incremental versions after 3.0, plus no delays, renaming, or shift in naming conventions. This tight timeline and the non‑negligible risk of a skip, delay, or a move to Gemini 4 make 99.3% overconfident; a probability near 90% is more realistic.
evidence_points: Google released Gemini 2.5 Pro (preview) in March 2025; a 3.0 launch is plausible by Q3‑Q4 2025.
Two further point releases (3.1, 3.2) within ~8 months is aggressive but possible; however, any slip or rebranding to a full version jump would cause a No resolution.
Public access via open beta/waitlist lowers the bar, but closed betas or limited early access would not qualify, adding execution risk.
